newsitem.title: UK: Clean tankers buoyant on good enquiry.
newsitem.headline: Clean tankers buoyant on good enquiry.

text.p: Clean tanker rates had a buoyant week with enquiries rising and signs that the market will remain firm until the end of the month, brokers said on Friday.
"Sufficient enquiry in virtually all areas enabled owners (this week) to find employment and, as the week progressed, there was increased interest in securing tonnage.
"It seems clear that the clean market is set firm until the forthcoming Easter break" next weekend, said brokers E.A. Gibson in their weekly tanker report.
They said most prompt medium range tonnage in the Middle East Gulf had now been fixed and rates were starting to rise.
Red Sea/India 40,000 tonne cargoes achieved W210, while 30,000 tonnes fetched W220 to west coast India.

Mideast/Japan 55,000 tonne vessels held roughly steady at W190, while smaller long range vessels from the Gulf that were still available in March were having to look to the Mediterranean for employment, Gibson said.
While Caribs/upcoast crude rates soared, the clean market was steady to weaker, with 40,000 tonnes fetching W200 -- flat despite a resurgence of enquiry mid-week, they added.
However, Caribs clean rates are still well above last year with 30,000 tonnes at W265 on Thursday.
That was against an average of W246 in 1996, according to New York-based Rigos Chartering Inc.
There was good interest in lifting product from the Med and Black Sea eastward, with the Elli reported fixed at a lumpsum of $1.3 million for 70,000 tonnes Black/Sea Singapore for Sinochem.

Brokers said inter-U.K./cont rates were steady with 20,000 tonnes fixed around W230/235 and there was also interest in moving larger cargoes of gas oil to Asia and unleaded gasoline to the U.S., but there were few actual fixtures.
